scope.current_boundary: Teach qualitative description and explanation of motion of objects in a uniform gravitational field with air resistance: initial release (t=0, v=0, D=0, a=g), speed increase, decreasing net force and acceleration, reaching terminal velocity (D=mg, a=0), comparative motion graphs (s-t, v-t, a-t) in air vs vacuum, factors affecting terminal velocity (mass, cross-sectional area, shape, fluid density), and skydiver lifecycle including parachute opening (upward net force and rapid deceleration to a second lower terminal velocity). Do not pre-teach multi-body systems, momentum conservation, or collisions.
prior_scope_summaries_consulted: Assumes mastery of lesson 9702_t03_cm01_l01: mass as inertia, F = ma.
Assumes mastery of lesson 9702_t03_cm01_l02: linear momentum, force as rate of change of momentum.
Assumes mastery of lesson 9702_t03_cm01_l03: Newton's three laws of motion, weight W = mg.
Assumes mastery of lesson 9702_t03_cm02_l04: frictional forces, fluid drag, simple model of drag increasing with speed.

immediate_previous.boundary: Frictional forces and viscous/drag forces including air resistance (simple model of drag increasing as speed increases, dependence on area and fluid).
can_assume: solid friction opposes relative motion and converts kinetic energy to thermal energy
drag force in fluids opposes relative velocity
drag is zero when speed is zero and increases as speed increases
drag increases with frontal cross-sectional area and fluid density
weight W = mg and resultant force F_net = ma

immediate_next.boundary: The principle of conservation of momentum: formal statement and application to collisions and explosions in 1D and 2D.
must_not_preteach: principle of conservation of linear momentum
isolated systems and external resultant forces
elastic vs inelastic collisions and relative speed of approach / separation

selection_dimensions: Components: P1 (multiple choice) and P2 (structured theory)
Years: 2016 to 2021 across February/March and May/June series
Archetypes: graph interpretation, explanation, comparison, direct calculation, property identification
Representations: velocity-time graphs in vacuum vs air, acceleration-time decay curves, acceleration vs air resistance lines, skydiver with parachute, falling stones of differing mass

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Directly compares the v-t graph in a vacuum (straight line, slope g) with the v-t graph in air (same initial slope, decreasing gradient, levels off at terminal velocity).
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Identify the correct velocity-time graph for an object falling in air on identical scales to vacuum free fall.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Must start with the same initial gradient g at t=0 because drag is zero at v=0, then bend over with decreasing gradient to a horizontal plateau.
lesson_sections_informed: Check 3: Initial gradient on a velocity-time graph
Mistake 5: Drawing a zero initial gradient on velocity-time graphs in air

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Verifies that at terminal velocity, acceleration is zero, gravity force is mg, and air resistance is mg.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: State the magnitude of gravity force, air resistance, and acceleration at terminal velocity.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Acceleration is zero, gravity force is mg, air resistance is mg. Gravity does not disappear.
lesson_sections_informed: Mistake 1: Believing gravity stops acting at terminal velocity

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Tests the shape of the acceleration-time graph for fall with air resistance, starting at g and decaying to zero.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Identify the acceleration-time graph for a tennis ball falling from rest in air.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Acceleration starts at g and decays smoothly toward zero as speed approaches terminal velocity.
lesson_sections_informed: Check 4: Acceleration-time graph for fall with air resistance

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Synthesizes multi-graph recognition: decaying curve is acceleration/force, rising-to-plateau curve is velocity.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Match physical quantities (velocity, acceleration, resultant force) to their graphical shapes against time.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Acceleration decays from max to zero; velocity rises from zero to plateau; resultant force has the same shape as acceleration (F = ma).
lesson_sections_informed: Graphical comparison: fall in a vacuum versus fall in air

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Addresses the classic parachutist misconception regarding velocity direction and magnitude after parachute opening.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Determine the direction and magnitude change of velocity immediately after parachute deployment.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Direction of velocity is still downwards; magnitude of velocity decreases.
lesson_sections_informed: Worked Example 2: Skydiver opening a parachute
Mistake 2: Thinking a skydiver shoots upwards when the parachute opens

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Explains why for two objects of the same dimensions, the lighter object reaches a lower terminal velocity and falls less distance in any time.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Identify the distance-time curve for a second stone of identical dimensions but smaller mass.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Smaller mass requires smaller drag to balance weight, reaching lower terminal velocity earlier.
lesson_sections_informed: Factors determining terminal velocity: Mass and weight
Worked Example 3: Comparing two falling spheres of different mass
Mistake 4: Believing heavy and light objects fall together in air

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Explores the linear relationship a = g - (1/m)D between downward acceleration and upward air resistance.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Identify quantities represented by a straight-line graph of negative slope for falling body with air resistance.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Plotting acceleration against air resistance gives a straight line with y-intercept g and slope -1/m.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Exam question testing why gradient of speed-time curve decreases: air resistance increases, net force and acceleration decrease.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: State and explain the variation with time of the gradient of speed-time graph when air resistance is not negligible.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Air resistance increases; resultant force and acceleration decrease, so gradient of the speed-time curve decreases.
